content: In this image I see a (black green blue) cable in the connector directly to the right of the y motor cable. On my machine that same connector port is empty, and the mentioned cable is plugged in one more space to the right. Is my set up wrong ?

replies.content:
I can't look this up on my printer right now as I'm not at home. but I think this doesn't matter. Originally the xBuddy board was developed for the MK4s which was a bed-slinger and thus had two z-axis motors (hence the two connectors). The CORE One though has three z-axis motors. So Prusa's solution was to add a stepper-splitter which splits one stepper motor signal into three (as seen in the MK4S -> CORE One Upgrade Guide:  https://help.prusa3d.com/guide/3-back-assembly_1004166#1007295).

The guide later instructs to connect the from the stepper-splitter to the right of those two connectors (labeled "ZR") as can be seen throughout the guide (see the wiring check for example: https://help.prusa3d.com/guide/7-bodywork-electronics_1004201#1019106).

In this guide here, that cable is just connected to the other socket.

Evidently it doesn't seem to matter, but yes, it would be less confusing for some if the pictures here were consistent with the previous guides.

@prusa: Maybe you could at least add a note to the text telling people that it's okay if the cable is connected to the other socket on their machine.

content: If your fingers are a little too large or fingernails too short to comfortably press the safety latch on the connectors (like mine are), I've had good luck using the end of one of the hex keys to depress the latch. The connector should come out with very little force with the latch depressed.
